source.note: Measured once during Phase 1 to derive timing only (countdown/reveal/transition/volume sections below). The file itself is not read by any production code and is not the source of the sfx assets -- those are restored from the project's earlier known-good implementation (commit 6e99c92), see the `sfx` section.

countdown.tickCountNote: Not the raw reference measurement below (measuredTicksPerGenuineRun=16) -- that count matched the reference video's own scene/duration structure, which this project does not use (production is fixed at 8 scenes / 7.25s max per scene, see config.js). tickCount here is instead FIT to the production scene structure's own countdown window: the pre-tick-train design's countdownStart-to-reveal span was 1.8112916666666667s, and at tickSpacingSeconds=0.2 plus the kept reveal.gapAfterLastTickSeconds=0.68, 6 ticks span 1.68s (the largest tick count that still fits inside that window -- 7 ticks would span 1.88s and overflow it). If the production scene structure changes, recompute this by hand; do not restore 16 without re-deriving it against whatever window is current at that time.
countdown.method: audio piped s16le mono 24000Hz through highpass=5500,lowpass=11000; RMS in 5ms windows; peaks above 97th percentile RMS with 0.09s minimum separation; consecutive peaks grouped into runs where spacing is 0.08-0.45s
countdown.excludedAnomaly: a 2-tick group at 35.850-35.965s (spacing 0.115s) did not fit the 16-tick pattern and was treated as noise, not a real countdown run -- excluded from the medians above

reveal.gapAfterLastTickSecondsNote: Overridden after production review (real rendered MP4) found the raw reference measurement below (0.68s) produced an audible ~0.6s dead-air gap between the last countdown tick and the reveal/result SFX -- both the reveal SFX and the visual percentage reveal are driven by this same value (see audio.js buildSceneTimeline revealTime, consumed by both buildSfxSchedule's 'reveal' event and media.js's percentAlpha), so they were already synchronized with each other; the gap itself was simply too large. Set to sfx.tick.durationSeconds (0.085s, below) so the reveal begins exactly as the last tick's own audible tail ends -- no dead air, no overlap. Do not restore 0.68 without re-justifying it against a real rendered review.
reveal.method: audio piped s16le mono 24000Hz through highpass=2400,lowpass=2900; RMS in 5ms windows; peaks above 99.3rd percentile RMS with 1.0s minimum separation; gap measured from each countdown run's last tick to the next reveal peak after it

transitions.blankDurationSecondsNote: Set to 0: the freeze-gap segment (media.js's buildFreezeGapSegment) is now redundant rather than removed outright -- scene N+1's entrance is baked directly into scene N's own segment tail as a single overlapping crossover transition (see media.js renderSegment's incoming-overlay block), so by the time scene N's segment ends, scene N+1's content is already fully in place. A freeze-gap hold afterward would just add unwanted extra dead time on top of an already-complete transition. Previously 0.2s; history kept here for context, not as a fallback value.
transitions.method: video scaled to 48x86 grayscale at 20fps, raw dump; spatial variance computed per frame; frames with variance below 1.3x the 5th percentile flagged as blank; consecutive blank frames grouped into runs

discardedReading.name: combinedTopAndBottomThirds
discardedReading.reason: the bottom third never drops below the blank threshold on its own -- it permanently holds the source video's TikTok logo and creator-handle overlay, which is an artifact of ref.mp4 being a downloaded post, not a property of the design being measured. Averaging it into the combined metric masked the real periodic pattern, which is only visible in the top third. Do not re-derive the combined reading; use topThirdOnly.

transitions.crossCheck: median interval independently computed from countdown-run start times (not the blank-frame detector) was 8.3225s, corroborating the 8.35s topThirdOnly reading

volume.method: ffmpeg -af volumedetect over the full file

sfx.note: Restored from the project's earlier known-good SFX implementation (commit 6e99c92, 'Finalize WYR media pipeline and content engine'), not synthesized and not extracted from reference/ref.mp4. Each asset's audio samples are bit-identical to that commit's original WAV; only the shipped container's own metadata (an embedded third-party platform video-ID tag -- see audio.test.js's leak-guard test) was stripped before installing, since it served no functional purpose and should never have been in shipped output. That embedded tag is evidence the original clip was extracted from a video the project owner posted; per the project owner it is unrelated to a separate, prior YouTube copyright block, which was caused by background music, not these SFX.

tick.description: single countdown tick, played once per tick event

reveal.description: result-reveal bell/chime sting with its full harmonic decay tail

whoosh.description: scene-transition whoosh, played on the outgoing edge of every non-final scene

slide.description: scene-entrance impact, played at the start of every scene

mix.loudnessNote: Final-output EBU R128 loudnorm target, applied once after the complete voice+SFX mix (see media.js buildAudioMixPlan) -- -14 LUFS integrated is the social-media loudness target; -1.5dBTP true-peak ceiling plus the trailing alimiter keep the result from ever clipping.
